key_insight: LLM judges detect unsafe clinical actions more reliably when given EHR evidence, but agent reasoning does not improve overall performance.
clinical_relevance: Clinical AI evaluation should check underlying actions and EHR evidence rather than rely on apparently successful final answers.
method: Injected eight categories of clinical errors into verified MedAgentBench trajectories.
Compared 416 faulty trajectories with correct counterparts using six open-weight LLM judges.
Varied access to final answers, full trajectories, EHR responses, and agent reasoning.
evidence_signal: Final-answer-only judges flagged 56% of correct trajectories; full-trajectory discrimination reached 0.75, while judges combined with an EHR-informed rule checker detected 97% of injected faults.
watch_item: These benchmark results use controlled fault injection and do not establish reliability in real-world clinical deployment.
paper_title: Can LLM Judges Catch Unsafe Clinical Actions? A Fault-Injection Study
